legend: Let T=(V,E)$$$T = (V, E)$$$ be a tree with n$$$n$$$ vertices and n−1$$$n-1$$$ edges. Each edge of the tree can be assigned a colour from {0,1,…,K−1}$$$\{0, 1, \dots, K-1\}$$$.

A simple path in a tree is called a K$$$K$$$-rainbow path if all edges along the path of length K$$$K$$$ have distinct colours. An edge is said to be K$$$K$$$-rainbow-valid if it lies on at least one K$$$K$$$-rainbow path. A tree is called a K$$$K$$$-tree if every edge in the tree is K$$$K$$$-rainbow-valid.

Your task is to assign colours to the edges of a given tree to form a K-tree with the largest possible K$$$K$$$. For each edge e$$$e$$$, you must report its assigned colour c(e)∈{0,1,…,K−1}$$$c(e) \in \{0, 1, \dots, K-1\}$$$ and the endpoints of a K-rainbow path that contains e$$$e$$$.
All indices are zero-based. If multiple valid colourings or paths exist, any may be output.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$ n $$$ (2≤n≤105)$$$(2 \leq n \leq 10^5)$$$. In the next n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines you are given the edges of the tree. In each of these lines you are given u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ (0≤u,v≤n−1)$$$(0 \leq u, v \leq n - 1)$$$ describing an edge between nodes u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$.
output: Your output must consist of n$$$n$$$ lines.
In the first line print the maximum possible K$$$K$$$.

In the next n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines, each line should contain three integers: c$$$c$$$, u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$, where 0≤c≤K−1$$$0 \leq c \leq K - 1$$$ and 0≤u,v≤n−1$$$0 \leq u, v \leq n - 1$$$. These integers specify the colour c$$$c$$$ of an edge and the path between u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$. This path includes the edge e$$$e$$$ and is a K-rainbow. The order of u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ does not matter.
Edges must be printed in the order they were given in the input.
